children: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty ended lower on Tuesday, snapping the Nifty’s four-day rally, as losses in IT, financial and capital goods stocks outweighed positive global cues and easing crude oil prices.
The BSE Sensex fell 329.91 points, or 0.44 per cent, to settle at 74,529.08 (touching an intraday low of  74,423.71), while the NSE Nifty declined 85.30 points, or 0.36 per cent, to end at 23,329.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, declined 1.67 per cent to $98.66 per barrel.

“Falling crude oil prices and softer global bond yields offered a more supportive backdrop, but the improvement in global conditions failed to translate into gains for Indian equities. The near-term bias remains cautiously weak, with market direction likely to hinge on whether domestic weakness persists despite an improving global backdrop,” said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, a SEBI-registered online trading and wealth tech firm.

Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments, said expectations of renewed diplomatic efforts surrounding the West Asia conflict and prospects of improved Saudi oil shipments eased concerns over inflationary pressures, while positive global cues lent additional support to the market.

“Sectoral performance remained mixed, reflecting a selective risk appetite among investors. With crude prices witnessing a sharp correction in recent weeks, market participants are increasingly focused on the sustainability of this trend given its implications for inflation, bond yields and corporate earnings,” Nair said.
Sectoral trend
Majority of the sectoral indices ended in negative territory. Media, Realty and Metal were the key gainers, while IT, FMCG and Banking were the major laggards.
The broader market also remained subdued, with the Nifty Smallcap 100 declining 0.26 per cent and the Nifty Midcap 100 falling 0.14 per cent.

Among Nifty 50 stocks, Coal India, IndiGo, Eternal, Titan and Dr Reddy’s Laboratories were the top gainers. Tata Consumer Products, Nestle, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Finance and Sun Pharmaceuticals were the major laggards.
Under the Nifty IT index, LTM, Persistent Systems, MphasiS, TCS and Infosys were the major losers.

A total of 3,670 stocks were traded on the NSE, of which 1,677 advanced, 1,867 declined and 126 remained unchanged. As many as 115 stocks scaled their 52-week highs, while 71 hit their 52-week lows. A total of 157 stocks scaled their upper circuits and 87 hit their lower circuits.
Global cues

In Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi, Shanghai’s SSE Composite index and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index ended marginally higher. European markets were trading in positive territory, while the US markets ended significantly higher on Monday.
“While geopolitical uncertainties remain unresolved, sustained stability in energy prices could improve earnings visibility and provide a firmer foundation for a broader market recovery,” Nair added.
FII selling
Foreign Institutional Investors offloaded equities worth ₹576.20 crore on Monday, according to exchange data.
Global brokerage Bernstein said foreign institutional investors (FIIs) may continue to trade in Indian equities but have limited reasons to make fresh investments.

Sunny Agrawal, Head - Fundamental Research at SBI Securities, said President Trump is scheduled to deliver his speech at the UN General Assembly tonight and Dow Futures were trading with gains of 120 points.
On Monday, the Sensex had jumped 564.03 points, or 0.76 per cent, to settle at 74,858.99. The Nifty had risen 67.90 points, or 0.29 per cent, to end at 23,414.30.
Key economic data to watch on Wednesday include the S&P Global Manufacturing and Services PMI readings.

title: Sensex, Nifty snap winning streak despite easing crude as IT, financials drag
